words.ex: He succumbs to pressure easily.
words.ex_cn: 他很容易屈服于压力。
words.en: If you succumb to temptation, pressure, or illness, you do something that you want to do, or you agree to do something that you do not want to do, or you die.

words.ex: He is learning agronomy at university.
words.ex_cn: 他正在大学学习农学。
words.en: Agronomy is the science of soil management and crop production.

words.ex: The imperial palace was built long ago.
words.ex_cn: 这座帝国宫殿是很久以前建造的。
words.en: relating to an empire or an emperor; majestic or superior in quality or size

words.ex: They placed a memorial at the site of the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他们在事故地点放置了一座纪念物。
words.en: A memorial is a structure or event established to remind people of a person or event.

words.ex: He reads science journals every week.
words.ex_cn: 他每周都读科学期刊。
words.en: A journal is a magazine, especially one that deals with a specialized subject, or a daily record of events or business.

words.tr: adj. 外部的；公开的；通俗的
words.ex: The teacher used exoteric language to explain the simple idea.
words.ex_cn: 老师用通俗的语言解释了这个简单的想法。
words.en: Intended for or likely to be understood by the general public; not esoteric or secret.

words.ex: The sanctity of life is a fundamental principle in many cultures.
words.ex_cn: 生命的神圣是许多文化中的一个基本原则。
words.en: The state or quality of being holy, sacred, or saintly.

words.tr:
n. 耻辱；丢脸；不光彩
v. 使丢脸；使蒙受耻辱
words.ex: He felt disgrace after lying to his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他向朋友撒谎后感到羞愧。
words.en: If you say that someone is in disgrace, you are emphasizing that other people disapprove of them and do not respect them because of something that they have done.

words.ex: The climates in northern countries are cold in winter.
words.ex_cn: 北欧国家的天气在冬天很冷。
words.en: The weather conditions prevailing in an area in general or over a long period.

words.tr: n. 冒险事业；商业冒险
words.ex: They are planning new business ventures in Asia.
words.ex_cn: 他们正在计划在亚洲进行新的商业冒险。
words.en: A venture is a project or activity that is new, exciting, and difficult because it involves the risk of failure.

words.tr:
adj. 积累的；积聚的；“amass”的现在分词
v. 积累；积聚；收集
words.ex: He is amassing a large collection of books.
words.ex_cn: 他正在积累大量的书籍。
words.en: To amass means to gather or accumulate a large amount of something, especially over a period of time.

words.tr: n. 康沃尔（英格兰西南部的一个郡）
words.ex: He lives in Cornwall with his family.
words.ex_cn: 他和家人住在康沃尔。
words.en: Cornwall is a county in the southwest of England, known for its rugged coastline, beautiful beaches, and historic mining towns.

words.ex: This box is the heaviest of all.
words.ex_cn: 这个箱子是所有箱子里最重的。
words.en: Superlative form of heavy; having the most weight.

words.ex: He is an optimist who believes things will get better.
words.ex_cn: 他是个乐观主义者，相信事情会好转。
words.en: An optimist is someone who always expects good things to happen or is always hopeful about the future.

words.ex: He outlined the plan in one sentence.
words.ex_cn: 他用一句话概述了这个计划。
words.en: To outline means to describe something in a general way, without giving all the details, or to draw the outer edge of something.

words.tr: adv. 确实，的确（古语或幽默用法）
words.ex: Forsooth, he did not know the answer.
words.ex_cn: 的确，他不知道答案。
words.en: An archaic or humorous term used to emphasize the truth of a statement, meaning 'indeed' or 'truly'.

words.ex: He discards old newspapers every week.
words.ex_cn: 他每周都丢弃旧报纸。
words.en: To discard something means to get rid of it because it is no longer useful or desirable.

words.tr: v. 下降；衰退；衰退（decline 的过去式和过去分词）；
words.ex: The number of visitors declined last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月访客数量下降了。
words.en: If something declines, it becomes less in quantity, importance, or strength.

words.tr:
adj. 聚精会神的
v. 集中；“focus”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: She remained focussed throughout the exam.
words.ex_cn: 她在整个考试过程中都保持专注。
words.en: If someone is focussed, they are giving all their attention to what they are doing.

words.tr: n. 抗议；反对；v. 抗议；反对
words.ex: People hold protests to demand change.
words.ex_cn: 人们举行抗议以要求变革。
words.en: Protests are public expressions of objection, disapproval, or dissent towards an idea or course of action, typically involving a group of people.

words.tr:
adv. 彻底地；立刻地；
adj. 完全的；彻底的；
words.ex: He refused the offer outright.
words.ex_cn: 他彻底拒绝了这个提议。
words.en: If something is done outright, it is done completely and without any hesitation or attempt to hide it.

words.tr: v. 帮助；援助；协助；“assist”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He assisted his friend with homework.
words.ex_cn: 他帮助朋友做作业。
words.en: If you assist someone, you help them to do a job or task by doing part of the work for them.

words.tr: n. 本杰明（男子名）；本杰明（圣经中的人物）；本杰明（一种植物）；
words.ex: Benjamin loves to play soccer with his friends.
words.ex_cn: 本杰明喜欢和朋友们踢足球。
words.en: Benjamin is a male given name, derived from the Hebrew name בִּנְיָמִין (Binyamin), meaning 'son of the right hand'. It is also the name of a plant and a character in the Bible.

words.ex: He went to the pawnshop to sell his watch.
words.ex_cn: 他去当铺卖他的手表。
words.en: A pawnshop is a shop where people can take things they own and leave them as security for money they have borrowed. If they do not pay the money back, the pawnshop can sell the items.

words.tr: n. 弗吉尼亚州（美国东部的一个州）；
words.ex: She lives in Virginia near the coast.
words.ex_cn: 她住在靠近海岸的弗吉尼亚州。
words.en: A state in the southeastern United States, known for its significant role in American history, including the first permanent English settlement at Jamestown.

words.tr: n. 推销员；售货员；“salesman”的复数
words.ex: The salesmen visited many customers last week.
words.ex_cn: 这些销售人员上周拜访了许多客户。
words.en: A salesman is a man whose job is to sell things, especially directly to shops or other businesses on behalf of a company.

words.ex: The audience gave applause after the song.
words.ex_cn: 歌曲结束后，观众鼓掌了。
words.en: Applause is the noise made by a group of people clapping their hands to show approval or enjoyment.

words.ex: He is grabbing his bag and leaving.
words.ex_cn: 他正抓起包准备离开。
words.en: To take or grasp something suddenly or quickly; to seize.

words.ex: The book is a masterful exercise in polemics, dissecting the arguments of both sides.
words.ex_cn: 这本书是辩论术的精湛练习，剖析了双方的论点。
words.en: The art or practice of engaging in controversial debate or dispute.

words.tr: n. 特价商品；协议，交易( bargain的名词复数 ) v. 讨价还价，商谈( bargain；
words.ex: She bought many bargains at the weekend sale.
words.ex_cn: 她在周末促销时买了许多特价商品。
words.en: Goods or services offered at a lower price than usual, often due to a sale or discount.

words.tr: n. 促进者；发起者；倡导者；支持者
words.ex: He is a promoter of healthy eating.
words.ex_cn: 他是健康饮食的倡导者。
words.en: A promoter is a person or organization that helps to organize and finance an event, such as a concert or sports match.

words.ex: She likes to follow new fashions.
words.ex_cn: 她喜欢追随新的时尚。
words.en: Fashions refer to the styles of clothing, hair, decoration, etc. that are popular at a particular time.

words.ex: We took an overland trip from Beijing to Moscow.
words.ex_cn: 我们从北京到莫斯科走了一条陆路旅行。
words.en: Relating to or denoting travel across the land, especially a long distance.

words.tr: v. 拷打；折磨；“torture”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: The tortured soul found no solace in his solitude.
words.ex_cn: 这个遭受精神折磨的灵魂在他的孤寂中找不到慰藉。
words.en: Experiencing or characterized by severe physical or mental suffering.

words.tr: adj. 负荷的; v. 把重担加于；劳累（burden 的过去分词）
words.ex: He was burdened with too much homework.
words.ex_cn: 他被太多的作业压得喘不过气。
words.en: If someone is burdened with something, they are carrying a heavy load of it, often something that is difficult to bear or that causes worry.

words.ex: He faced many hardships during the war.
words.ex_cn: 他在战争期间经历了许多困苦。
words.en: Hardship refers to a situation that is difficult to endure because of lack of money, resources, or other basic necessities.

words.tr: n. 建造；竖立；建筑物；（阴茎）勃起
words.ex: The erection of the new building took six months.
words.ex_cn: 新大楼的建造花了六个月。
words.en: The act of building or constructing something; the state of being built or constructed; also refers to the physiological process in males.

words.ex: The gatherer collected wild berries from the forest.
words.ex_cn: 采集者从森林里采摘野莓。
words.en: A gatherer is someone who collects things, especially plants or food, from the wild.

words.ex: My neighbor gives me apples from her tree.
words.ex_cn: 我的邻居从她的树上给我摘苹果。
words.en: A neighbor is someone who lives near you, or a country that is next to another country.

words.tr: adj. 奥地利的；奥地利人的；
words.ex: He bought an Austrian violin at the market.
words.ex_cn: 他在市场上买了一把奥地利的小提琴。
words.en: Relating to Austria or its people.

words.tr: n. 弟兄们；同胞；教友；会友
words.ex: The brethren gathered for prayer each morning.
words.ex_cn: 兄弟们每天早上聚集祷告。
words.en: Brethren is an old-fashioned plural form of 'brother', used especially in religious contexts to refer to male members of a group or community.

words.ex: There is a large variance between the budget and the actual cost.
words.ex_cn: 预算与实际成本之间有很大的差额。
words.en: Variance refers to the fact or quality of being different, divergent, or inconsistent.

words.ex: The examiner asked the student a difficult question.
words.ex_cn: 考官问了学生一个难题。
words.en: An examiner is a person who checks something carefully in order to see if it is correct or satisfactory, or who gives people a test to see what they know or can do.

words.ex: The usurpers took the throne by force.
words.ex_cn: 篡位者用武力夺取了王位。
words.en: A usurper is someone who takes a position of power or importance illegally or by force.

words.tr: v. 取代；迫使…离开家园；
words.ex: The new robot will displace the workers on the assembly line.
words.ex_cn: 这个新机器人将取代装配线上的工人。
words.en: To displace something or someone means to take their place or to force them to leave their usual place or role.

words.ex: The police hold inquests to find out how people die.
words.ex_cn: 警方举行死因调查以查明人们的死亡原因。
words.en: An inquest is an official process to find out the cause of someone's death, especially when it is sudden or suspicious.

words.ex: He furthers his knowledge by reading every day.
words.ex_cn: 他通过每天阅读来增进自己的知识。
words.en: To help something to develop or be successful.

words.ex: The sheep graze on the highland.
words.ex_cn: 羊在高地上吃草。
words.en: Highland refers to an area of high or mountainous land, often characterized by its elevation above sea level and distinct geographical features.

words.ex: He became the champion of the tennis tournament.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得了网球锦标赛的冠军。
words.en: A champion is someone who has won first prize in a competition, contest, or fight.

words.ex: He has a delusion that he is a famous singer.
words.ex_cn: 他有一种错觉，认为自己是一位著名歌手。
words.en: A delusion is a belief or impression that is firmly maintained despite being contradicted by what is generally accepted as reality or rational argument, typically a symptom of mental disorder.

words.tr: adv. 得体地；正派地；相当好地
words.ex: She dressed decently for the interview.
words.ex_cn: 她为了面试穿得很得体。
words.en: In a decent manner; properly or adequately.

words.ex: He quit his job because of coercion from his boss.
words.ex_cn: 他因为老板的强迫而辞了工作。
words.en: The act of persuading someone to do something by using force or threats.

words.ex: The creature lived in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这个生物生活在森林里。
words.en: A creature is a living thing, especially an animal.

words.tr: adj. 鲁莽的；厚颜的；冒失的；放肆无礼的
words.ex: The impudent boy talked back to his teacher.
words.ex_cn: 这个鲁莽的男孩顶撞了老师。
words.en: If you describe someone as impudent, you mean they are rude or disrespectful, or they show a lack of shame about their behavior.

words.tr: n. 素描；速写；草图；草图( sketch的名词复数 )；
words.ex: He showed me his sketches of mountains.
words.ex_cn: 他给我看了他的山景素描。
words.en: A sketch is a simple, quickly-made drawing that does not have many details. It can also refer to a short description or outline of a plan or idea.

words.ex: He snatched the bag and ran away.
words.ex_cn: 他抢过包就跑了。
words.en: To take something quickly and often rudely or roughly.

words.ex: The book has clear headings for each chapter.
words.ex_cn: 这本书的每一章都有清晰的标题。
words.en: A heading is a title at the head of a page or section of a book, or the direction in which a ship or aircraft is moving.

words.ex: He hesitates to ask for help.
words.ex_cn: 他犹豫着是否要寻求帮助。
words.en: If you hesitate, you pause slightly while you are doing something or just before you do it, usually because you are uncertain, embarrassed, or worried.

words.tr: adj. 人口众多的；人口密集的
words.ex: China is a populous country.
words.ex_cn: 中国是一个人口众多的国家。
words.en: If a place is populous, it has a large population.

words.ex: He is devoting time to learn English.
words.ex_cn: 他正在花时间学习英语。
words.en: To give all or a large part of one's time or resources to a particular activity, person, or cause.

words.ex: He insisted on going home early.
words.ex_cn: 他坚持要早点回家。
words.en: To demand something forcefully, not accepting refusal.

words.tr: adj. 笨拙的； v. “bungle”的现在分词；
words.ex: The bungling clerk dropped the files everywhere.
words.ex_cn: 这个笨拙的职员把文件撒得到处都是。
words.en: If you describe someone's actions as bungling, you mean that they are clumsy, awkward, or inefficient.

words.ex: The teacher will announce the results tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 老师明天将宣布结果。
words.en: To announce something means to make it known publicly or officially.

words.ex: The teacher mediates disputes between students.
words.ex_cn: 老师调解学生之间的纠纷。
words.en: To mediate means to intervene between people or parties in order to bring about an agreement or reconciliation.

words.ex: The epidemic spread quickly across the country.
words.ex_cn: 这种流行病迅速蔓延到全国。
words.en: An epidemic is a large number of cases of an infectious disease occurring at the same time.

words.ex: The dutchman sailed his boat across the sea.
words.ex_cn: 那个荷兰人驾船横渡了大海。
words.en: A Dutchman is a man who comes from the Netherlands.

words.ex: He picked up the receiver to answer the phone.
words.ex_cn: 他拿起听筒接电话。
words.en: A receiver is a person who receives something or a device that receives signals and converts them into sound or pictures.

words.tr: adv. 顺利地；平稳地；顺畅地；
words.ex: The machine works smoothly.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器运行顺利。
words.en: In a smooth manner; without problems or difficulties.

words.ex: The boy resembles his father.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩长得像他父亲。
words.en: If one thing or person resembles another, they are similar to each other.

words.ex: The fluidity of the liquid made it easy to pour.
words.ex_cn: 液体的流动性使其易于倾倒。
words.en: The quality of being able to change or be changed easily.

words.ex: The movie was mediocre and not worth watching.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影很平庸，不值得看。
words.en: If you describe something as mediocre, you mean that it is of average quality but you think it should be better.

words.tr: n. （美）[畜牧]大草原（prairie 的复数）
words.ex: The cows graze on the prairies.
words.ex_cn: 牛群在大草原上吃草。
words.en: A prairie is a large open area of grassland, especially in North America.

words.ex: The trees surround the house.
words.ex_cn: 树木环绕着房子。
words.en: If something or someone is surrounded by something, that thing is situated all around them.

words.tr: adj. 地狱的；恶魔似的；可憎的
words.ex: The heat in the room was infernal.
words.ex_cn: 房间里的热量像地狱一样。
words.en: If you describe something as infernal, you are emphasizing that it is extremely annoying or unpleasant.

words.tr: adj. 假情假义的；油腔滑调的
words.ex: His unctuous manner made me uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他油腔滑调的态度让我感到不舒服。
words.en: If you describe someone as unctuous, you are critical of them because they seem to be full of praise, kindness, or interest, but in a way that is not sincere.

words.ex: The pitiable dog had no home.
words.ex_cn: 那只可怜的狗没有家。
words.en: Deserving or arousing pity.

words.tr:
adv. 在海外；在国外；
adj. 海外的；
words.ex: He moved overseas for work.
words.ex_cn: 他为了工作搬到了海外。
words.en: If something is overseas, it is in a foreign country, usually separated from your own country by an ocean.

words.ex: They are residing in a small house near the park.
words.ex_cn: 他们正住在公园附近的一所小房子里。
words.en: To reside means to live in a particular place or to exist in a particular state or condition.

words.ex: He lives in Portugal.
words.ex_cn: 他住在葡萄牙。
words.en: Portugal is a country located on the Iberian Peninsula in southwestern Europe, known for its maritime history, cultural heritage, and as the birthplace of port wine.

words.tr: n. 运转; 运行; 活动方式; （已开采过的）矿坑
words.ex: The workings of the machine were clearly visible.
words.ex_cn: 机器的运转情况清晰可见。
words.en: The workings of something are the parts of it which allow it to function or operate.

words.tr: adj. 傲慢的；无礼的；侮慢的
words.ex: The insolent boy talked back to his teacher.
words.ex_cn: 那个无礼的男孩顶撞了老师。
words.en: If you say that someone is insolent, you mean they are rude and do not show respect for people in positions of authority.

words.ex: The train goes over the viaducts in the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 火车从山上的高架桥上驶过。
words.en: A viaduct is a long, high bridge, usually with arches, that carries a road or railway across a valley or other low area.

words.tr: v. 狼吞虎咽地吃；贪婪地阅读
words.ex: He devoured the book in one sitting.
words.ex_cn: 他一口气读完了那本书。
words.en: To eat hungrily or quickly; to read or look at something with great interest and enthusiasm.

words.tr: adj. 最遥远的；最偏僻的
words.ex: That village is the remotest place I have ever seen.
words.ex_cn: 那个村庄是我见过的最偏远的地方。
words.en: Superlative form of 'remote', meaning the most distant or far away in space or time.

words.ex: The worker had long exposure to loud noise.
words.ex_cn: 这名工人长期暴露在噪音中。
words.en: The condition of being exposed to something, especially to something harmful or unpleasant.

words.tr: n. 凑整；凑整（round 的现在分词）； v. 使变圆；
words.ex: The calculator uses rounding to show two decimal places.
words.ex_cn: 计算器使用凑整来显示两位小数。
words.en: Rounding refers to the process of adjusting a number to a nearby value that is easier to work with or understand, often to a specific degree of accuracy.

words.tr:
n. 提倡者；
v. 提倡；
words.ex: He is an advocate for clean water.
words.ex_cn: 他是清洁用水的提倡者。
words.en: If you advocate a particular action or plan, you recommend it publicly.

words.ex: The noblemen lived in big castles long ago.
words.ex_cn: 很久以前，贵族们住在大城堡里。
words.en: Noblemen are men of high social rank or title, typically in a hereditary system.

words.tr: v. 大批杀死；大量毁灭
words.ex: The storm decimated the village.
words.ex_cn: 风暴摧毁了这个村庄。
words.en: To decimate something such as a group of people or animals means to destroy a very large number of them.

words.ex: His attitude toward homework is very positive.
words.ex_cn: 他对作业的态度非常积极。
words.en: An attitude is a way of thinking or feeling about something, which is often reflected in a person's behavior.

words.ex: He proposes a new method for solving the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他提出了一种解决问题的新方法。
words.en: If you propose something, you suggest it as a plan or course of action.

words.ex: The electric lamp lights up the room.
words.ex_cn: 电灯照亮了房间。
words.en: Something that is electric works by means of electricity, is powered by electricity, or produces electricity.

words.ex: He has a strong physique from lifting weights.
words.ex_cn: 他因为举重而拥有强健的体格。
words.en: The form, size, and development of a person's body.

words.ex: Carbonic acid breaks down into water and CO2.
words.ex_cn: 碳酸分解成水和二氧化碳。
words.en: Relating to or containing carbon, especially in the form of carbon dioxide.

words.tr: adj. 品行端正的；品德高的；
words.ex: He is a virtuous man who always tells the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个品行端正的人，总是说真话。
words.en: Having or showing high moral standards.

words.ex: He is diligent in doing his homework every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都很勤奋地做作业。
words.en: Someone who is diligent works hard and is careful and thorough.

words.tr: adj. 到期的；即将结束的
words.ex: The milk is expiring tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 这瓶牛奶明天过期。
words.en: Coming to an end or reaching the end of its validity.

words.ex: The kids are the changers in this game.
words.ex_cn: 这些孩子是这个游戏中的变化者。
words.en: Changers are individuals or entities that bring about change or exchange in a particular context.

words.ex: Many people go to churches on Sundays.
words.ex_cn: 很多人在星期天去教堂。
words.en: Churches are buildings used for Christian religious activities, especially worship services.

words.ex: The solstice happens in June and December.
words.ex_cn: 夏至和冬至分别发生在六月和十二月。
words.en: The solstice is the time of the year when the sun is at its greatest distance from the celestial equator, occurring around June 21 and December 21.

words.tr: v. 削弱；变弱；“weaken”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The storm weakened the old bridge.
words.ex_cn: 风暴削弱了这座旧桥。
words.en: Made or become less strong or powerful.

words.tr:
n. 伪装；伪装物；
v. 伪装；掩饰；
words.ex: He wore a hat and glasses as a disguise.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了帽子和眼镜作为伪装。
words.en: To disguise means to change your appearance or behavior so that people will not recognize you, or to make something seem different from what it really is.

words.ex: I have a meeting on Thursday.
words.ex_cn: 我星期四有一个会议。
words.en: Thursday is the day of the week between Wednesday and Friday.

words.ex: The judge condemns the thief for stealing.
words.ex_cn: 法官因偷窃而谴责小偷。
words.en: To express strong disapproval of someone or something, typically in public; to sentence someone to a particular punishment, especially death.

words.ex: The strange noise confounded the children.
words.ex_cn: 奇怪的声音让孩子们感到困惑。
words.en: To confuse and surprise someone, especially by being difficult to understand or deal with.

words.ex: The vagabond sleeps under the bridge.
words.ex_cn: 这个流浪汉睡在桥下。
words.en: A vagabond is someone who wanders from place to place without a home or job.

words.tr: adj. 教诲的；说教的；好教训人的
words.ex: The teacher gave a didactic speech to help students learn.
words.ex_cn: 老师发表了一篇富有教育意义的演讲来帮助学生学习。
words.en: Something that is didactic is intended to teach people something, especially a moral lesson.

words.tr: n. 穷困; 痛苦( misery的名词复数 ); 痛苦的事; 常发牢骚的人
words.ex: The miseries of the poor families made the community cry.
words.ex_cn: 穷困家庭的悲惨境况让整个社区都落泪了。
words.en: Great suffering, distress, or hardship.

words.ex: The settlers built houses near the river.
words.ex_cn: 殖民者在河边建造了房屋。
words.en: Settlers are people who go to live in a new country or area.

words.ex: Paul wrote epistles to early Christian churches.
words.ex_cn: 保罗给早期的基督教教会写了书信。
words.en: An epistle is a letter, especially a formal or didactic one; it is often used to refer to the letters in the New Testament written by the apostles.

words.ex: The fog obscures the road ahead.
words.ex_cn: 雾气遮蔽了前方的路。
words.en: To make something unclear or difficult to understand or see.

words.ex: The workers load stone from the quarries.
words.ex_cn: 工人们从采石场装载石头。
words.en: A quarry is a place, typically a large, deep pit, from which stone or other materials are or have been extracted. It can also refer to an animal or person that is being hunted or chased.

words.tr: adj. 技艺精湛的，熟练的
words.ex: He played the piano in a masterly way.
words.ex_cn: 他以高超的方式弹奏钢琴。
words.en: A masterly action or performance is done very skillfully.

words.tr: adj. 使人惊恐的；引起恐慌的； v. “alarm”的现在分词；
words.ex: The news report showed an alarming rise in crimes.
words.ex_cn: 新闻报道显示犯罪率令人惊恐地上升。
words.en: If something is alarming, it makes you feel afraid or anxious that something unpleasant or dangerous might happen.

words.tr: adj. 持久的；不朽的； v. 忍受；“endure”的现在分词；
words.ex: This is an enduring friendship.
words.ex_cn: 这是一段持久的友谊。
words.en: Lasting for a long time; continuing or enduring over a period of time.

words.ex: The earthquake was a terrible calamity.
words.ex_cn: 这场地震是一场巨大的灾难。
words.en: A calamity is an event that causes great harm or damage, such as a flood or a fire.

words.ex: The doctor gave him an antidote for the poison.
words.ex_cn: 医生给了他一种解毒剂来对抗毒药。
words.en: An antidote is a substance that counteracts the effects of poison or something harmful.

words.tr: v. 过滤；“filter”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The water was filtered before drinking.
words.ex_cn: 水在饮用前被过滤了。
words.en: Having been passed through a filter to remove impurities or unwanted material.

words.ex: They levelled the ground before building the house.
words.ex_cn: 他们在建房子之前把地面弄平了。
words.en: To make something flat or even; to make something equal or fair; to aim or direct something.

words.ex: Parental love is very important for children.
words.ex_cn: 父母的爱对孩子非常重要。
words.en: Relating to or characteristic of a parent or parents.

words.ex: He is blacking the shoes with polish.
words.ex_cn: 他正在用鞋油擦鞋。
words.en: A substance used to blacken or polish something, especially shoes.

words.ex: He works in a vineyard near the hills.
words.ex_cn: 他在山边的一个葡萄园工作。
words.en: A vineyard is a plantation of grape-bearing vines, grown mainly for winemaking, but also raisins, table grapes and non-alcoholic grape juice.

words.ex: He works at a colliery in the north.
words.ex_cn: 他在北方的一个煤矿工作。
words.en: A colliery is a coal mine and all the buildings and equipment associated with it.

words.ex: The country has an agrarian economy.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家有一个农业经济。
words.en: Relating to land, especially agricultural land, or to the ownership or division of such land.

words.ex: The city is widening the road to reduce traffic.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市正在加宽道路以减少交通拥堵。
words.en: The process of becoming wider or making something wider.

words.tr: v. 强加；“impose”的现在分词； adj. 壮观的；
words.ex: He imposed his rules on the team.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的规则强加给团队。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as imposing, you mean that they have an impressive appearance or manner.

words.ex: The dog's docility made it easy to train.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗的温顺使它容易训练。
words.en: The quality of being easily taught, led, or managed; submissiveness.

words.ex: The employee arrived at work early.
words.ex_cn: 这位雇员早早到达了工作地点。
words.en: An employee is a person who is paid to work for an organization or for another person.

words.tr: n. 重击；重创；痛击； v. “pound”的现在分词；
words.ex: The pounding of the drums scared the children.
words.ex_cn: 鼓声的重击吓到了孩子们。
words.en: The act of hitting something repeatedly with great force.

words.tr: adj. 繁荣的；旺盛的；兴旺的； v. 兴旺；繁荣；茁壮成长；“thrive”的现在分词；
words.ex: The town is thriving because of its new factories.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇因为新的工厂而繁荣。
words.en: Prospering or flourishing; successful.

words.ex: The omission of his name was an accident.
words.ex_cn: 他的名字被漏掉是无意的。
words.en: An omission is something that has not been included or has not been done, either deliberately or accidentally.

words.ex: The overseers watch the workers every day.
words.ex_cn: 监工们每天监督工人们。
words.en: A person who supervises others, especially workers.

words.tr: n. 自然增加；增加之物；增值
words.ex: The accretion of sand formed a small beach.
words.ex_cn: 沙子的堆积形成了一个小海滩。
words.en: Accretion is the process of growth or increase, typically by the gradual accumulation of additional layers or matter.

words.ex: He subjoined a note to the letter.
words.ex_cn: 他在信后附上了一则注释。
words.en: To add or append something, especially at the end of a document or text.

words.ex: The bills are totalling $500 this month.
words.ex_cn: 这个月的账单总计500美元。
words.en: To add up the total of something.

words.tr: n. 坚定不移；持久不变
words.ex: His constancy never changes, even when things are hard.
words.ex_cn: 他的坚定从不改变，即使事情很艰难。
words.en: The quality of being unchanging or unwavering, especially in one's loyalty or affections.

words.ex: Eating vegetables gives you good nutrition.
words.ex_cn: 吃蔬菜能提供良好的营养。
words.en: The process of providing or obtaining the food necessary for health and growth.

words.tr: v. 徘徊；漫游；“wander”的现在分词；
words.ex: He was wandering in the park after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚饭后在公园里徘徊。
words.en: If you describe a person or their thoughts as wandering, you mean that the person is not concentrating on anything in particular and their thoughts are not clear.

words.ex: She was immensely happy after winning the prize.
words.ex_cn: 她赢得奖品后极大地开心。
words.en: To an extremely great extent or degree.

words.ex: His lectures were marked by erudition and wit.
words.ex_cn: 他的讲座以博学和机智著称。
words.en: Erudition is the quality of having or showing great knowledge or learning.

words.ex: Water can penetrate the soil slowly.
words.ex_cn: 水可以慢慢渗透进土壤。
words.en: To penetrate means to enter or pass through something, especially when this is difficult or when it is not obvious how to do it.

words.ex: His inability to swim saved him from drowning.
words.ex_cn: 他不会游泳，这救了他一命。
words.en: If you refer to someone's inability to do something, you are emphasizing that they cannot do it.

words.tr: n. 难以理解的事；古代的秘密宗教仪式（mystery 的复数）；
words.ex: The mysteries of the deep ocean still confuse scientists.
words.ex_cn: 深海的难以理解的事仍然让科学家困惑。
words.en: Mysteries are things that are not understood or known about, often because they are difficult to understand or explain.

words.ex: The artist is enlarging the photograph to make a poster.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家正在放大照片制作海报。
words.en: To make something bigger or more extensive.

words.tr:
adj. 爆炸的；
n. 炸药；
words.ex: The explosive material was handled with care.
words.ex_cn: 爆炸性材料被小心地处理。
words.en: An explosive substance is capable of causing an explosion. It can also refer to something that is likely to cause an outburst or a sudden increase in activity or emotion.

words.ex: He regretted leaving his job too soon.
words.ex_cn: 他后悔太早辞掉了工作。
words.en: If you regret something that you have done, you wish that you had not done it.

words.tr:
v. 移动；操控；
n. （熟练地）移动；
words.ex: He manoeuvred the car into a small parking space.
words.ex_cn: 他把车开进了一个小停车位。
words.en: A manoeuvre is a movement or series of movements requiring skill and care, especially in military tactics or in driving a vehicle. It can also refer to a clever or cunning plan or action designed to turn a situation to one's own advantage.

words.tr: adv. 不相等地；不公平地
words.ex: They unequally divided the cookies.
words.ex_cn: 他们不平等地分了饼干。
words.en: In a manner that is not equal or fair.

words.tr: v. <正>开始( commence的第三人称单数 )
words.ex: The class commences at 8 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 课程在早上8点开始。
words.en: Begins or starts.

words.tr: adj. 有活力的；精力旺盛的；
words.ex: The energetic boy ran around the park all afternoon.
words.ex_cn: 这个有活力的男孩整个下午都在公园里跑来跑去。
words.en: Someone who is energetic is very active and does not tire easily.

words.tr: adj. 有组织的； v. 组织；“organize”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: She is an organized student who keeps her books in order.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个有条理的学生，把书整理得井井有条。
words.en: If something is organized, it is arranged in an orderly, efficient way.

words.ex: The drawbacks of this phone are high price and short battery.
words.ex_cn: 这款手机的缺点是价格高和电池续航短。
words.en: A drawback is a feature that makes something less effective than it could be.

words.ex: The ticket is your admission to the concert.
words.ex_cn: 这张票是进入音乐会的许可。
words.en: An admission is a statement in which you admit that something bad, unpleasant, or embarrassing is true, or the act of allowing someone to enter a place or organization.

words.ex: I couldn't apprehend the math lesson because it was too fast.
words.ex_cn: 我无法理解这节数学课，因为讲得太快了。
words.en: If the police apprehend someone, they catch them and arrest them.

words.tr: n. 冠军；拥护者 v. 支持；拥护
words.ex: The champions won the match last night.
words.ex_cn: 冠军们昨晚赢得了比赛。
words.en: A champion is someone who has won a competition, especially a sports competition, or someone who strongly supports a particular cause or person.

words.ex: She showed great affection for her little dog.
words.ex_cn: 她对她的小狗非常钟爱。
words.en: A feeling of liking and caring for someone or something.

words.tr: n. 伪装；掩饰 v. 伪装；掩饰
words.ex: He wears disguises to hide from the police.
words.ex_cn: 他戴着伪装来躲避警察。
words.en: To disguise means to change the appearance or sound of someone or something so that they cannot be recognized.

words.tr: n. 厚颜无耻；无礼；放肆
words.ex: His impudence surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的无礼让所有人都感到惊讶。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as impudence, you mean it is rude and disrespectful.

words.tr: n. [数] 倍数；跨国公司；多倍制图仪；连票
words.ex: He listed the multiples of five: five, ten, fifteen.
words.ex_cn: 他列出了五的倍数：五、十、十五。
words.en: Multiples refer to the product of a quantity by an integer. In finance, it often refers to the ratio of a company's stock price to its earnings per share.

words.tr: v. 下降；衰退；“decline”的现在分词； adj. 衰退的；下滑的；
words.ex: The number of students is declining each year.
words.ex_cn: 学生人数每年都在下降。
words.en: If something is declining, it is becoming less in quantity, importance, or strength.

words.tr: n. 装饰品（ornament 的复数）
words.ex: She put ornaments on the Christmas tree.
words.ex_cn: 她把装饰品挂在圣诞树上。
words.en: An ornament is an object that is used to decorate or embellish something, making it more attractive.

words.tr: v. 使降级；使降职；把…归类
words.ex: He was relegated to the bench after the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他在犯错后被换到了替补席上。
words.en: To assign to an obscure place, position, or condition; to send or consign to an inferior position, place, or condition.

words.tr: n. 指数；拥护者；说明者
words.ex: He learned exponents in math class.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学课上学了指数。
words.en: An exponent is a person who supports or explains a particular idea or theory, or a mathematical notation indicating the power to which a number is to be raised.

words.tr: v. 发生；“happen”的现在分词； n. 事件；偶然发生的事；
words.ex: What is happening now?
words.ex_cn: 现在发生了什么？
words.en: an event or occurrence

words.tr: v. 改善；改进；“improve”的现在分词； n. 改善；改进；
words.ex: He is improving his English every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都在改善他的英语。
words.en: If something improves or if you improve it, it gets better.

words.ex: The ministers discussed the new policy in the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 部长们在会议上讨论了新政策。
words.en: A minister is a person who is in charge of a particular government department, or a member of the clergy, especially in Protestant churches.

words.tr: n. 幸存者；残存物；遗风
words.ex: The survivals of ancient tools show early human life.
words.ex_cn: 古代工具的遗存展示了早期人类的生活。
words.en: Survivals refer to people or things that continue to exist or function, especially in difficult conditions or after a disaster.

words.ex: He confesses that he made a mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他承认自己犯了一个错误。
words.en: To admit or acknowledge something, especially something that one is ashamed of or that might be damaging to oneself.

words.ex: The company sends weekly shipments to customers.
words.ex_cn: 公司每周向客户发货。
words.en: Shipments refer to the goods that are being transported from one place to another, especially in large quantities.

words.tr: n. 摘要；抽象概念；抽象艺术作品
words.ex: He reads science abstracts every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上阅读科学摘要。
words.en: An abstract is a summary of a text or a concept that is not concrete.

words.tr:
adj. 疏远的；不和的；分居的
v. 使疏远；使分离；“estrange”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He is estranged from his family.
words.ex_cn: 他与家人疏远了。
words.en: If someone is estranged from their family or friends, they have had a serious argument and are no longer friendly with them.

words.tr: n. 登记（表）( register的名词复数 ); 记录器; 暖气; 自动记录器 v. 注册; 登
words.ex: The registers of births, deaths, and marriages are kept at the town hall.
words.ex_cn: 出生、死亡和结婚的登记簿保存在市政厅。
words.en: 1. A book or record of entries, events, or names. 2. To officially record something, especially in a book or on a list.

words.ex: He swallowed the pill with water.
words.ex_cn: 他用水把药片吞了下去。
words.en: To cause food, drink, or something else to pass from the mouth through the throat and into the stomach.

words.ex: The phone has had many volutions since 2000.
words.ex_cn: 自2000年以来，这部手机经历了许多变革。
words.en: A volution is a rolling or revolving motion, or a single turn or twist in a spiral or coil.

words.tr: v. 顺从；顺从( submit的过去式和过去分词 )；
words.ex: He submitted to the teacher's rules.
words.ex_cn: 他顺从了老师的规则。
words.en: If you submit to something, you unwillingly allow something to be done to you, or you do what someone wants, for example because you are not powerful enough to resist.

words.ex: The town has three small breweries.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇有三家小型啤酒厂。
words.en: A brewery is a place where beer is made commercially.

words.ex: The shortness of the breath made him stop running.
words.ex_cn: 呼吸的短促让他停下了跑步。
words.en: The condition of being short in duration, length, or stature; lack of sufficient quantity.

words.ex: There is a disparity in pay between men and women.
words.ex_cn: 男女之间的工资存在差异。
words.en: A disparity between two or more things is a noticeable difference between them.

words.tr: adj. 孤立的；绝缘的; v. 使隔离；使绝缘（isolate 的 ing 形式）
words.ex: The pandemic has made many people feel isolating.
words.ex_cn: 疫情让许多人感到孤立。
words.en: If you describe a place or situation as isolating, you mean that it makes you feel alone and unable to meet or communicate with other people.

words.ex: He was defrauded of his inheritance by a dishonest lawyer.
words.ex_cn: 他被一个不诚实的律师骗走了他的遗产。
words.en: To defraud means to illegally obtain money from someone by deceiving them.

words.tr: adj. 分子的；分子构成的；
words.ex: Water is a molecular compound.
words.ex_cn: 水是一种分子化合物。
words.en: Relating to or consisting of molecules.

words.ex: The immigrant found a job in the city.
words.ex_cn: 这位移民在城市里找到了一份工作。
words.en: An immigrant is a person who comes to live permanently in a foreign country.

words.tr: v. 作曲；撰写；“compose”的现在分词；
words.ex: He is composing a song for his daughter.
words.ex_cn: 他正在为女儿作一首歌。
words.en: The act of creating or putting together something, especially a piece of music or writing.

words.tr: n. 稳健；坚固性；健全；公正
words.ex: The soundness of the structure was questioned by the engineers.
words.ex_cn: 工程师们对该结构的稳固性提出了质疑。
words.en: The quality or state of being sound; especially, the state of being free from defect, decay, or damage; firmness; solidity; validity.

words.ex: He testified in court about what he saw.
words.ex_cn: 他在法庭上作证，讲述了他所看到的事情。
words.en: To testify means to make a formal statement, especially in a court of law, about something that you have seen, heard, or experienced.

words.tr: v. 使（某物）更明亮( lighten的过去式和过去分词 ); 变得更光明
words.ex: The sun lightened the sky at dawn.
words.ex_cn: 黎明时，太阳使天空变亮了。
words.en: To make or become lighter or less heavy; to make or become less dark or less serious.

words.tr: adj. 无价值的；不值钱的；微不足道的
words.ex: The old toy is valueless now.
words.ex_cn: 这个旧玩具现在没有价值。
words.en: Having no value; worthless.

words.tr: v. 把…归因于；把…归属于
words.ex: He is ascribing the mistake to carelessness.
words.ex_cn: 他把错误归因于粗心。
words.en: To attribute something to a particular cause or source.

words.ex: The publisher released a new book last month.
words.ex_cn: 出版者上个月发布了一本新书。
words.en: A publisher is a person or company that prepares and issues books, journals, or music for sale.

words.tr:
n. 极端；最大限度
adj. 极端的；最远的
words.ex: He pushed himself to the uttermost.
words.ex_cn: 他把自己推向了极限。
words.en: The greatest degree or amount; the furthest limit.

words.tr: v. 解决；决定（ resolve的现在分词 ）；
words.ex: They are resolving the conflict peacefully.
words.ex_cn: 他们正在和平地解决这场冲突。
words.en: The process of finding a solution to a problem or conflict.

words.ex: He felt indignant when they blamed him for the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 当他们把错误归咎于他时，他感到愤愤不平。
words.en: If you are indignant, you are shocked and angry, because you think that something is unjust or unfair.

words.ex: The fireworks at night were a beautiful spectacle.
words.ex_cn: 夜晚的烟花是一场美丽的奇观。
words.en: A spectacle is a visually striking performance or display.

words.ex: He is a temperate person who never shouts.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个温和的人，从不大喊大叫。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as temperate, you mean that it is calm and reasonable, not extreme or emotional.

words.ex: He proclaims his love every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都宣告他的爱。
words.en: If someone proclaims something, they formally announce or declare it, often publicly.

words.ex: The company recruited five new employees last month.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司上个月招募了五名新员工。
words.en: If you recruit people for an organization, you select them and persuade them to join it or work for it.

words.tr: adj. 遮蔽的；受庇护的；受保护的； v. 庇护；遮蔽；“shelter”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The children played in a sheltered garden.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在一处遮蔽的花园里玩耍。
words.en: Protected from the harsh realities of life; not exposed to difficulties or unpleasantness.

words.ex: He displayed his photos on the wall.
words.ex_cn: 他把照片展示在墙上。
words.en: If you display something, you show it to people, or put it in a place where people can see it easily.

words.ex: He is an architect who designs houses.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位设计房屋的建筑师。
words.en: An architect is a person who designs buildings and advises in their construction.

words.tr: adj. 骇人的； v. “appall”的现在分词；
words.ex: The accident caused an appalling sight.
words.ex_cn: 这场事故造成了一幅骇人的景象。
words.en: If you describe something as appalling, you are emphasizing that it is very bad or unpleasant, and that you find it extremely unacceptable.

words.tr: v. 养肥（fatten 的现在分词）; adj. 使人发胖的；正被养肥的；用于养肥禽畜的
words.ex: Sugary snacks are fattening.
words.ex_cn: 甜点心容易让人发胖。
words.en: Making or becoming fat or fatter.

words.ex: Dogs follow their instincts to protect their owners.
words.ex_cn: 狗遵循它们保护主人的本能。
words.en: Innate, intuitive behaviors or responses not learned through experience.

words.ex: The weather was tolerable, so we went for a walk.
words.ex_cn: 天气还可以忍受，所以我们去散步了。
words.en: If something is tolerable, it is acceptable or bearable, even though it is not very good or pleasant.

words.ex: Loud noise aggravates his headache.
words.ex_cn: 噪音加重了他的头痛。
words.en: If someone or something aggravates a situation, they make it worse.

words.ex: I recommend this book to you.
words.ex_cn: 我向你推荐这本书。
words.en: If someone recommends a person or thing to you, they suggest that you would find them good or useful.

words.tr: n. 原件; 原文( original的名词复数 ); [the original] 原型; 原型人
words.ex: The originals of these documents are kept in the archive.
words.ex_cn: 这些文件的原件保存在档案馆。
words.en: Originals are works of art or documents that are not copies but were created by the artist or author themselves.

words.ex: The two parties formed a coalition to win the election.
words.ex_cn: 这两个政党联合起来以赢得选举。
words.en: A coalition is a temporary alliance for combined action, especially of political parties forming a government.

words.tr: adj. 法定的；依照法规的；
words.ex: The statutory minimum wage is $10 per hour.
words.ex_cn: 法定最低工资是每小时10美元。
words.en: Statutory means relating to rules or laws which have been formally written down.

words.ex: The law restricts driving after midnight.
words.ex_cn: 法律限制午夜后开车。
words.en: If something restricts you, it limits or controls what you can do.

words.ex: He is insisting on going alone.
words.ex_cn: 他坚持要独自去。
words.en: To insist means to demand something forcefully, not accepting refusal.

words.ex: He convinces his friends to join the club.
words.ex_cn: 他让朋友们同意加入这个俱乐部。
words.en: To make someone believe that something is true or to persuade someone to do something.

words.ex: The aforesaid rule applies to all students.
words.ex_cn: 上述规则适用于所有学生。
words.en: Used to refer to something that has already been mentioned.

words.tr: v. 是…的迹象；作证( witness的过去式和过去分词 )；
words.ex: The dry soil witnessed a long drought.
words.ex_cn: 干裂的土壤是长期干旱的迹象。
words.en: To see something happen, especially a crime or accident.

words.tr:
adj. 第十六的；
n. 第十六；
num. 第十六；
words.ex: He finished in sixteenth place in the race.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛中获得了第十六名。
words.en: The ordinal number matching the number 16 in a series.

words.tr: v. 生成；（通过物理或化学过程）发生；
words.ex: The machine generates electricity.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器发电。
words.en: Creates or produces something, especially as a result of a process or action.

words.ex: The spokesman spoke clearly at the press conference.
words.ex_cn: 发言人在新闻发布会上清晰地发言。
words.en: A spokesman is a man who speaks on behalf of a group or an organization.

words.ex: He is an unmarried man who lives alone.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个独居的未婚男子。
words.en: Not married; single.

words.ex: The UN is mediating between the two warring factions.
words.ex_cn: 联合国正在两个交战派系之间进行调停。
words.en: To mediate means to intervene between people or groups in order to bring about an agreement, a settlement, or a reconciliation.

words.ex: We need better solutions for clean water.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要更好的清洁用水的解决办法。
words.en: A solution to a problem or difficult situation is a way of dealing with it so that the difficulty is removed.

words.ex: The equation has two variables, x and y.
words.ex_cn: 这个方程有两个变量，x 和 y。
words.en: In mathematics and programming, a variable is a symbol used to represent an unknown or changeable value.

words.ex: The children saw the cruelties of war on TV.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在电视上看到了战争的残酷。
words.en: Cruelties refer to acts of extreme unkindness or harshness, often causing suffering or pain to others.

words.ex: The teacher criticise the student for not doing homework.
words.ex_cn: 老师批评学生没有做作业。
words.en: If you criticise someone or something, you express your disapproval of them by saying what you think is wrong with them.

words.ex: The old foundries made iron parts for machines.
words.ex_cn: 旧的铸造厂为机器制造铁制零件。
words.en: A foundry is a factory where metal is melted and poured into molds to make metal objects.

words.ex: The teacher gave formative feedback to help students improve.
words.ex_cn: 老师给出了影响形成的学习反馈，以帮助学生改进。
words.en: Relating to or characterized by the formation or development of something.

words.ex: The doctor prescribed medicine for my cold.
words.ex_cn: 医生给我开了治疗感冒的药。
words.en: If a doctor prescribes medicine or treatment for you, he or she tells you what medicine or treatment to have.

words.tr: n. 呼吸； v. 呼吸；“breathe”的现在分词；
words.ex: Deep breathing helps you relax.
words.ex_cn: 深呼吸有助于你放松。
words.en: The process of taking air into the lungs and expelling it; a sign of life.

words.ex: He is a collector of old coins.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位古钱币收藏家。
words.en: A collector is a person who collects things of a particular type as a hobby or for investment.

words.ex: He was caught snatching a purse from an old lady.
words.ex_cn: 他被抓到时正从一位老太太那里抢钱包。
words.en: To take something or someone quickly and often rudely or roughly.

words.ex: The butterfly emerged from its chrysalis.
words.ex_cn: 蝴蝶从它的蛹中出来了。
words.en: A chrysalis is the hard-shelled pupa of a butterfly or moth, typically motionless and often camouflaged.

words.tr: n. 钞票，纸币( banknote的名词复数 )
words.ex: He took out a bundle of banknotes from his wallet.
words.ex_cn: 他从钱包里拿出了一叠钞票。
words.en: A banknote is a piece of paper money, especially one issued by a central bank.

words.ex: We picked mushrooms in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 我们在森林里采了蘑菇。
words.en: Mushrooms are fungi that typically have a stem, a cap, and gills on the underside of the cap. They can be found in various environments and are used in cooking for their flavor and texture.

words.tr: v. <拉>商谈，商议( confer的过去式和过去分词 ); 授予，赋予
words.ex: They conferred about the plan last night.
words.ex_cn: 他们昨晚商议了这个计划。
words.en: If you confer something such as a degree, award, or right on someone, you give it to them.

words.ex: We eat at mealtimes together as a family.
words.ex_cn: 我们一家人在一起吃饭时间吃饭。
words.en: Mealtimes refer to the times at which meals are usually eaten.

words.tr: adj. 饱和的； v. “saturate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The sponge was saturated with water.
words.ex_cn: 海绵被水浸透了。
words.en: If something is saturated, it is completely soaked with liquid or has absorbed as much of a substance as it can.

words.tr: v. 加工；处理；“process”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 加工过的；经加工的；
words.ex: The factory processes milk into cheese.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂将牛奶加工成奶酪。
words.en: If something is processed, it has been treated with a particular method or substance in order to preserve it, improve its appearance, or make it suitable for use.

words.ex: He is earnestly trying to learn English.
words.ex_cn: 他正在认真地学习英语。
words.en: In a serious and sincere manner.

words.tr: n. 野蛮；原始；未开化；暴虐
words.ex: The soldier was punished for his barbarism during the war.
words.ex_cn: 那名士兵因在战争中的野蛮行为而受到惩罚。
words.en: Barbarism refers to the state of being uncivilized or the act of being extremely cruel or brutal.

words.tr:
adj. 怪诞的；丑陋奇异的；奇形怪状的
n. 奇形怪状的东西；奇异风格
words.ex: The painting showed a grotesque face with twisted eyes.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画上有一个扭曲眼睛的怪诞面孔。
words.en: If you say that something is grotesque, you mean that it is extremely unattractive, exaggerated, and often shocking or disturbing.

words.ex: He is fortunate to have a good job.
words.ex_cn: 他很幸运拥有一份好工作。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is fortunate, you mean that they are lucky.

words.ex: The towel is absorbent and dries quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这条毛巾能吸水，干得快。
words.en: An absorbent material is able to take in liquids easily.

words.tr: v. 承担；从事；“undertake”的过去式；
words.ex: He undertook the project alone.
words.ex_cn: 他独自承担了这个项目。
words.en: If you undertake a task or responsibility, you start doing it and accept responsibility for it.

words.ex: The medicine is relieving her pain.
words.ex_cn: 这种药正在缓解她的疼痛。
words.en: Relieving means to make something less severe, intense, or painful.

words.tr: v. 坚持自己的主张；声称( assert的现在分词 )；
words.ex: He is asserting his right to speak.
words.ex_cn: 他正在坚持自己发言的权利。
words.en: If you assert a fact or belief, you state it firmly and confidently.

words.ex: Her actions were purposive and deliberate.
words.ex_cn: 她的行为是有目的且故意的。
words.en: Having or done with a purpose; intentional.

words.tr: n. 寡头政治；寡头统治集团；寡头统治的国家
words.ex: The country is ruled by an oligarchy of wealthy businessmen.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家由一群富有的商人寡头统治。
words.en: A form of government in which all power is vested in a few persons or in a dominant class or clique; government by the few.

words.tr: n. 勒索；强夺；恐吓取财
words.ex: The police are investigating allegations of extortion.
words.ex_cn: 警方正在调查有关勒索的指控。
words.en: Extortion is the crime of obtaining something from someone, especially money, by using force or threats.

words.ex: The teacher elucidated the math problem with a simple diagram.
words.ex_cn: 老师用一个简单的图表阐明了这道数学题。
words.en: To make something clear or easy to understand by explaining or giving reasons.

words.ex: He helped extricate the car from the mud.
words.ex_cn: 他帮助把车从泥里解脱出来。
words.en: If you extricate someone or something from a place where they are trapped or caught, you succeed in freeing them.

words.tr: v. 准备； adj. 准备的，预备的 v. 准备( prepare的现在分词 )；
words.ex: He is preparing for his exam.
words.ex_cn: 他正在为考试做准备。
words.en: If you prepare something, you make it ready for something that is going to happen.

words.ex: The embryonic stage is the earliest phase of development.
words.ex_cn: 胚胎阶段是发育的最早时期。
words.en: In an early stage of development; rudimentary.

words.ex: The cavaliers won the basketball game last night.
words.ex_cn: 骑士队昨晚赢了篮球比赛。
words.en: Cavaliers are men who are gallant and chivalrous, often associated with knights or those who support a monarch.

words.ex: Kindness engenders trust.
words.ex_cn: 善良培养信任。
words.en: To cause a feeling, situation, or condition to exist.

words.ex: The teacher is assigning homework to the students.
words.ex_cn: 老师正在给学生们布置作业。
words.en: To allocate or designate someone or something for a particular purpose or task.

words.ex: The goldsmith made a beautiful ring.
words.ex_cn: 金匠做了一个漂亮的戒指。
words.en: A goldsmith is a person who makes, repairs, or sells articles made of gold.

words.tr: n. 就职；即位；正式加入
words.ex: The king's accession was celebrated by the whole nation.
words.ex_cn: 国王的登基受到了全国的庆祝。
words.en: The act of attaining or gaining access to a position, right, or status.

words.ex: He handed out pamphlets about health.
words.ex_cn: 他分发了关于健康的宣传册。
words.en: A pamphlet is a small booklet or leaflet containing information or arguments about a single subject.

words.ex: The incipient fire was put out quickly.
words.ex_cn: 初期的小火被迅速扑灭了。
words.en: An incipient situation or quality is one that is just beginning to develop or become noticeable.

words.ex: He will surrender when he sees the police.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到警察时，他会投降。
words.en: If you surrender, you stop fighting or resisting someone and agree that you have been beaten.

words.ex: Many hospitals are busy during winter.
words.ex_cn: 许多医院在冬天都很忙。
words.en: A hospital is an institution where sick or injured people are given medical or surgical care.

words.ex: Eating too much sugar is unhealthy.
words.ex_cn: 吃太多糖是不健康的。
words.en: If you describe something as unhealthy, you mean that it is likely to cause illness or poor health.

words.ex: The bonus is an incentive to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 奖金是努力工作的动机。
words.en: Something that encourages a person to do something or to work harder.

words.ex: The cat resembles a tiger.
words.ex_cn: 这只猫像老虎。
words.en: If one thing or person resembles another, they are similar to each other.

words.tr:
n. 共产主义者；
adj. 共产主义的；
words.ex: He is a communist who believes in equal sharing of wealth.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名相信财富平等分配的共产主义者。
words.en: A communist is a person who believes in communism, which is a political system that aims for a classless society in which the means of production are owned communally and private property is nonexistent or severely curtailed.

words.tr: adj. 赤贫的；贫困的；一无所有的；
words.ex: The destitute family had no food or shelter.
words.ex_cn: 这个赤贫的家庭没有食物和住所。
words.en: If you describe someone as destitute, you mean they have absolutely nothing, especially no money.

words.ex: He got an exemption from paying the fee.
words.ex_cn: 他获得了免交费用的豁免。
words.en: An exemption is an official permission not to do something or not to pay something that you would normally have to do or pay.

words.tr: v. 建议；暗示；提出；“suggest”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He suggested a new plan.
words.ex_cn: 他建议了一个新计划。
words.en: If you suggest something, you put forward a plan or idea for someone to think about.

words.ex: The stripping of paint revealed the old wood underneath.
words.ex_cn: 油漆的剥离露出了下面的旧木头。
words.en: The act of removing something from a surface or the act of taking off clothes.

words.tr: n. 历史遗迹；纪念碑；“monument”的复数；
words.ex: Many tourists visit ancient monuments in Rome.
words.ex_cn: 许多游客参观罗马的古代历史遗迹。
words.en: A monument is a structure, statue, or building that is built to honor a special person or event.

words.ex: There are frictions between the two teams.
words.ex_cn: 两个团队之间有摩擦。
words.en: Frictions refer to the resistance that one surface or object encounters when moving over another, or the conflict or disagreement between people or groups.

words.ex: He worked intensely to finish the project.
words.ex_cn: 他强烈地工作以完成这个项目。
words.en: If something is intense, it is very great or extreme in strength or degree.

words.tr: vt. 摧毁；大幅度下降；大幅度下降（decimate 的过去式及过去分词）；
words.ex: The storm decimated the village.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴摧毁了村庄。
words.en: To destroy, remove, or severely damage a large proportion of something.

words.ex: He works in marketing for a tech company.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家科技公司从事营销工作。
words.en: Marketing involves the process of promoting, selling, and distributing a product or service. It includes market research and advertising.

words.tr: adj. 叛乱的; 背叛的; 使人厌恶的 v. 使厌恶(revolt的现在分词形式); 反叛，背叛
words.ex: The food was so revolting that I couldn't eat it.
words.ex_cn: 这食物太令人作呕了，我吃不下去。
words.en: If you say that something or someone is revolting, you mean you think they are horrible and disgusting.

words.tr: v. 受益；得到好处；“benefit”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He benefited from the new program.
words.ex_cn: 他从这个新项目中受益了。
words.en: To derive advantage or gain; to be helped by something.

words.tr: n. 婚姻；结合；兼并（marriage 的复数）
words.ex: Many marriages end in divorce after five years.
words.ex_cn: 许多婚姻在五年后以离婚告终。
words.en: Marriages refer to the legally or formally recognized union of two people as partners in a personal relationship.

words.ex: The harvested wheat was stored in the barn.
words.ex_cn: 收获的小麦被存放在谷仓里。
words.en: To harvest means to gather a crop or to receive the benefits of something after a period of effort or work.

words.ex: He acted in the pursuance of his duty.
words.ex_cn: 他按照职责行事。
words.en: The act of pursuing or carrying out a plan or task.

words.tr: n. 单元住宅；公寓住宅；
words.ex: He lives in a small apartment near the park.
words.ex_cn: 他住在公园附近的一间小公寓里。
words.en: An apartment is a set of rooms for living in, usually on one floor of a large building.

words.tr: adj. 不顾一切的；极度渴望的；绝望的；
words.ex: He made a desperate attempt to save the child.
words.ex_cn: 他不顾一切地试图救那个孩子。
words.en: If you are desperate, you are in such a bad situation that you are willing to try anything to change it.

words.tr: adj. 反复出现的；再发生的；
words.ex: He has recurrent headaches every week.
words.ex_cn: 他每周都反复出现头痛。
words.en: Happening or appearing again or repeatedly.

words.ex: The visa application requires a lot of formality.
words.ex_cn: 签证申请需要很多正式手续。
words.en: A formality is something that is done as part of a formal process or procedure, often without much thought or feeling because it is expected.

words.tr: n. 混合; 混合物; 掺和; 附加剂
words.ex: He added an admixture of salt to the soup.
words.ex_cn: 他往汤里加了一点盐混合物。
words.en: An admixture is a combination of different things, especially when this is unusual or unexpected.

words.tr: n. 无稽之谈；胡言乱语
words.ex: He spoke gibberish, making it impossible to understand his message.
words.ex_cn: 他语无伦次，让人无法理解他的意思。
words.en: If you describe someone's words or ideas as gibberish, you mean that they do not make any sense.

words.tr: adj. 滋养的；养育( nourish的过去式和过去分词 )；
words.ex: The nourished plants grew tall and strong.
words.ex_cn: 这些得到滋养的植物长得又高又壮。
words.en: If someone is nourished, they are provided with the food and other substances that are necessary for life, growth, and good health.

words.ex: The firefighters brought salvation to the people trapped in the burning building.
words.ex_cn: 消防员拯救了被困在着火大楼里的人们。
words.en: Salvation is the act of saving or protecting from harm, risk, loss, destruction, etc., or the state of being saved from such conditions.

words.ex: The two brothers have many conflicts.
words.ex_cn: 这两个兄弟有很多冲突。
words.en: A conflict is a serious disagreement or argument, typically a protracted one.

words.ex: Jesus had twelve disciples who followed him.
words.ex_cn: 耶稣有十二个门徒跟随他。
words.en: A disciple is a person who follows and learns from a teacher or leader, especially in a religious context.

words.ex: The watch works with great precision.
words.ex_cn: 这块手表运行得非常精确。
words.en: Precision is the quality of being exact and accurate.

words.tr:
v. 建造；构造；
n. 概念；
words.ex: They construct houses with bricks.
words.ex_cn: 他们用砖块建造房屋。
words.en: To construct something means to build or create it, usually something large such as a building, road, or machine.

words.tr: v. 尽全力； n. 变形，应变 v. 拉紧( strain的现在分词 )；
words.ex: He is straining to lift the heavy box.
words.ex_cn: 他正尽全力举起这个重箱子。
words.en: The act of stretching or pulling tight; a force tending to pull or stretch something.

words.ex: He is reselling old books online.
words.ex_cn: 他正在网上转卖旧书。
words.en: The act of selling something that one has bought, typically for a profit.

words.tr: n. 先见；预见；先见之明
words.ex: He showed foresight by saving money for the future.
words.ex_cn: 他通过为未来存钱展现了远见。
words.en: The ability to predict or the action of predicting what will happen or be needed in the future.

words.ex: The police found evidences at the crime scene.
words.ex_cn: 警察在犯罪现场找到了证据。
words.en: Facts or information indicating whether a belief or proposition is true or valid.

words.ex: He interprets the poem as a love story.
words.ex_cn: 他把这首诗解释为一个爱情故事。
words.en: If you interpret something in a particular way, you decide that this is its meaning or significance.

words.ex: His argument was full of sophistry, making it difficult to discern the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点充满了诡辩，让人难以分辨真相。
words.en: Sophistry is the use of clever but false arguments, especially with the intention of deceiving.

words.ex: He speaks three languages fluently.
words.ex_cn: 他能流利地说三种语言。
words.en: Languages refer to the system of communication used by a particular community or country, consisting of words used in a structured and conventional way and conveyed by speech, writing, or gesture.

words.tr: n. 出庭律师；法律顾问
words.ex: The barrister spoke clearly in court.
words.ex_cn: 律师在法庭上清晰地发言。
words.en: A barrister is a type of lawyer in the UK and some other countries who has the right to speak and argue as an advocate in higher law courts.

words.tr:
adj. 反复的；重复的；循环的
v. 重复；重做；“repeat”的现在分词
words.ex: The repeating pattern on the wallpaper creates a sense of continuity.
words.ex_cn: 墙纸上重复的图案营造出一种连续感。
words.en: Doing or saying something again.

words.ex: The commander gave the order to advance.
words.ex_cn: 指挥官下达了前进的命令。
words.en: A commander is a person in authority, especially in the armed forces, who gives orders and is responsible for the actions of those under their command.

words.ex: The economies of many countries are growing slowly.
words.ex_cn: 许多国家的经济增长缓慢。
words.en: Economies refer to the system by which a country's money, goods, and services are produced and used, or the careful management of resources to avoid waste.

words.ex: We arrived at the opportune moment, just as the meeting was starting.
words.ex_cn: 我们到达得很及时，正好会议刚开始。
words.en: If something happens at an opportune time or is opportune, it happens at the time that is most convenient for someone or most likely to lead to success.

words.ex: The pipes are made of metal cylinders.
words.ex_cn: 这些管道由金属圆柱体制成。
words.en: A cylinder is a geometric figure with straight parallel sides and a circular or oval cross section.

words.tr: n. 谄媚者，拍马屁的人
words.ex: The king surrounded himself with sycophants.
words.ex_cn: 国王身边围绕着一群阿谀奉承的人。
words.en: Sycophants are people who praise powerful or rich people in a way that is not sincere, in order to gain some advantage for themselves.

words.ex: He has a preference for tea over coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他更喜欢茶而不是咖啡。
words.en: A preference is a greater liking for one alternative over another or others.

words.tr: adj. 学院的；学业的；学术的；教学的
words.ex: He received a scholastic award for top grades.
words.ex_cn: 他因成绩优异获得了学院奖。
words.en: Relating to schools and education.

words.ex: The child wears restraints in the car for safety.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在车里系着安全约束装置以确保安全。
words.en: Restraints are limits or controls that are placed on something or someone to prevent them from doing something or to limit their actions.

words.tr: v. 禁止；不准；“forbid”的现在分词；
words.ex: The sign forbids parking here.
words.ex_cn: 这个标志禁止在这里停车。
words.en: If you describe something as forbidding, you mean it has a severe, unfriendly, or threatening appearance.

words.ex: He lives in Washington.
words.ex_cn: 他住在华盛顿。
words.en: Washington refers to the capital city of the United States, the state of Washington in the United States, or George Washington, the first President of the United States.

words.ex: He spoke eloquently about justice.
words.ex_cn: 他雄辩地谈论了正义。
words.en: In a manner that is fluent and persuasive in speaking or writing.

words.ex: He works hard to support his dependents.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作来养活他的家属。
words.en: A dependent is a person who relies on another, especially a family member, for financial support.

words.tr:
adj. 个性强势的
v. 统治；支配；“dominate”的现在分词
words.ex: He is dominating the game with his skills.
words.ex_cn: 他凭借自己的技巧主导着比赛。
words.en: Having a commanding influence on; exercising control or power over.

words.ex: The carpenters built a wooden table.
words.ex_cn: 木匠们做了一张木桌。
words.en: A carpenter is a person whose job is making and repairing wooden objects and structures.

words.tr: n. 承办者；承担者；殡葬承办人；殡仪员
words.ex: The undertaker arranged the funeral with great care.
words.ex_cn: 殡仪业者非常细心地安排了葬礼。
words.en: An undertaker is a person whose job is to manage funerals and prepare the bodies of dead people for burial or cremation.

words.ex: He performed remarkably well in the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他在考试中表现得非常出色。
words.en: In a way that is worthy of attention; strikingly.

words.ex: Travellers carry maps to find their way.
words.ex_cn: 旅行者带着地图找路。
words.en: People who are travelling or who often travel.

words.tr: v. 面向；举向；（分娩时婴儿）露出；举向( present的现在分词 )；
words.ex: The classroom is presenting toward the north.
words.ex_cn: 这个教室面向北方。
words.en: The act of showing or offering something for others to see or consider.

words.tr: n. 萃取，提取，提炼 v. 提取( extract的现在分词 ); （费力地）拔出; 选取; 获得
words.ex: He is extracting data from the spreadsheet.
words.ex_cn: 他正在从电子表格中提取数据。
words.en: To remove or take out something, especially by effort or force.

words.tr: v．; 1. 推测，猜测：对未知事物进行思考或猜测。; 2. 投机：以期望获得利润为目的进行投资或交...
words.ex: He speculates that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他推测明天会下雨。
words.en: If someone speculates about something, they make guesses about its nature or identity, or about what might happen.

words.ex: The divergence of opinions caused a big argument.
words.ex_cn: 意见的背离导致了一场激烈的争论。
words.en: A divergence is a difference between two or more things, attitudes, or opinions.

words.tr: adj. 加强的； v. 增强；“reinforce”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The concrete wall is reinforced with steel bars.
words.ex_cn: 这堵混凝土墙用钢筋加固了。
words.en: To reinforce something means to make it stronger or more able to withstand pressure, especially by adding extra material or support.

words.tr: n. 摧毁；拆毁；拆除；大败；
words.ex: The demolition of the old building started last week.
words.ex_cn: 那座旧楼的拆除上周开始了。
words.en: The act of demolishing something, especially a building.

words.ex: He behaves peculiarly when he is nervous.
words.ex_cn: 当他紧张时，他的行为很奇怪。
words.en: In a manner that is unusual or distinctive; particularly.

words.tr: v. 包围；围绕；“surround”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 被…环绕着的；
words.ex: The house is surrounded by trees.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子被树木包围着。
words.en: If you are surrounded by something, it is all around you.

words.tr: adj. 值得注意的；显著的；
words.ex: This result is noteworthy because it changes our understanding.
words.ex_cn: 这个结果值得注意，因为它改变了我们的理解。
words.en: If you describe something as noteworthy, you mean that it is interesting, significant, or important enough to deserve attention or to be noticed.

words.tr:
adj. 深思熟虑的；故意的；
v. 深思熟虑；
words.ex: He made a deliberate choice to quit his job.
words.ex_cn: 他深思熟虑后决定辞去工作。
words.en: If you do something that is deliberate, you planned or decided to do it beforehand, and so it happens on purpose rather than by chance.

words.tr: adj. 不适宜的；不合适的；
words.ex: This shirt is unsuitable for the cold weather.
words.ex_cn: 这件衬衫不适合寒冷的天气。
words.en: If someone or something is unsuitable for a particular purpose or situation, they are not appropriate for it.

words.ex: The god was incarnated as a human.
words.ex_cn: 这位神明化身为人。
words.en: To incarnate means to embody or represent something in a tangible or visible form, often referring to the manifestation of an idea, spirit, or deity in human or physical form.

words.tr: v. 提出（理论、计划等）供考虑
words.ex: He propounded a new theory last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年提出了一个新理论。
words.en: To propound means to put forward or offer for consideration, acceptance, or adoption; set forth; propose.

words.tr: adj. 执拗的；难驾驭的；难以治愈的
words.ex: The refractory material can withstand high temperatures.
words.ex_cn: 这种耐火材料能承受高温。
words.en: Stubbornly resistant to authority or control; difficult to melt or work; resistant to heat.

words.tr: n. 擒纵机构；擒纵轮；擒纵装置；
words.ex: The clock's escapement controls the movement of the gears.
words.ex_cn: 钟表的擒纵机构控制齿轮的运动。
words.en: A mechanism in a clock or watch that controls the speed of the gear train and thus the movement of the hands, or any similar mechanism that controls movement.

words.ex: The line is horizontal on the graph.
words.ex_cn: 这条线在图上是水平的。
words.en: Parallel to the plane of the horizon; at right angles to the vertical.

words.ex: The fireworks caused loud explosions in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 烟花在夜空中引发了巨大的爆炸。
words.en: An explosion is a sudden, violent burst of energy, for example one caused by a bomb.

words.tr: n. 对手；对立者；对抗者
words.ex: The antagonist in the story is a greedy king.
words.ex_cn: 故事中的反派是一个贪婪的国王。
words.en: An antagonist is someone who opposes another person.

words.tr: adj. 易接近的；可使用的；简单易懂的；可进入的；
words.ex: The park is accessible by bus.
words.ex_cn: 这个公园乘公交车可达。
words.en: If a place or building is accessible to people, it is easy for them to reach it or get into it. If an object is accessible, it is easy to reach.

words.tr: adv. 无论什么；任何(用于否定句中以加强语气)；
words.ex: You can eat whatever food whatsoever.
words.ex_cn: 你可以吃任何食物。
words.en: used to emphasize a negative statement

words.ex: Phosphorus is in some fertilizers.
words.ex_cn: 磷存在于一些肥料中。
words.en: Phosphorus is a chemical element with the symbol P and atomic number 15. It is a nonmetal that is essential for life, found in DNA, RNA, ATP, and the phospholipids that form all cell membranes.

words.ex: The map has an indicative arrow to show the way.
words.ex_cn: 这张地图上有一个指示方向的箭头。
words.en: If one thing is indicative of another, it suggests what the other thing is likely to be.

words.ex: He is protecting the environment by recycling.
words.ex_cn: 他通过回收利用来保护环境。
words.en: If you protect someone or something, you prevent them from being harmed or damaged.

words.tr: n. 出版（业）；出版社； v. 发布；出版；“publish”的现在分词；
words.ex: He works in publishing.
words.ex_cn: 他在出版业工作。
words.en: Publishing is the profession or business of producing and selling books, magazines, or newspapers.

words.tr: v. 反映；反思；反射；“reflect”的现在分词；
words.ex: The lake is reflecting the mountains.
words.ex_cn: 湖面映出了山峦。
words.en: If a surface reflects light, heat, or sound, it sends the light, etc. back and does not absorb it. If something reflects an attitude or situation, it shows that the attitude or situation exists or it shows what it is like.

words.tr: n. 地方法官；治安官；行政官；
words.ex: The magistrate decided the small case quickly.
words.ex_cn: 地方法官迅速裁决了这起小案件。
words.en: A magistrate is an official who acts as a judge in law courts that deal with minor crimes or disputes.

words.ex: He signed the guarantees before receiving the loan.
words.ex_cn: 他在收到贷款前签署了保证书。
words.en: A guarantee is a formal promise that something will be done or will happen, especially a written promise by a company to repair or change a product that develops a fault within a particular period of time.

words.ex: He was criticised for being late.
words.ex_cn: 他因为迟到而受到批评。
words.en: If you criticise someone or something, you express your disapproval of them by saying what you think is wrong with them.

words.tr: v. 使溶解； adj. v. 使溶解（dissolve 的现在分词）；
words.ex: Sugar is dissolving in hot water.
words.ex_cn: 糖正在热水中溶解。
words.en: If a substance dissolves in a liquid, or if you dissolve it, it becomes mixed with the liquid and disappears.

words.tr: n. 话语; 论文( discourse的名词复数 ); 演说; 讲道
words.ex: He reads many discourses on politics.
words.ex_cn: 他阅读许多关于政治的论述。
words.en: Written or spoken communication or debate; to speak or write about a topic in detail.

words.ex: The war led to the decimation of the village population.
words.ex_cn: 这场战争导致了该村人口的大批杀害。
words.en: The act of killing or destroying a large part of a group or population.

words.tr: adj. 流传甚广的；分布广的；
words.ex: The flu became widespread last winter.
words.ex_cn: 去年冬天流感流传甚广。
words.en: Something that is widespread exists or happens over a large area, or to a great extent.

words.tr: adv. 密切地；亲密地；谙熟地；
words.ex: They are intimately connected by family ties.
words.ex_cn: 他们通过家庭关系密切相连。
words.en: In a way that involves a close link or relationship; closely.

words.ex: He understands difficult situations easily.
words.ex_cn: 他很容易理解复杂的情况。
words.en: Situations refer to the set of circumstances in which one finds oneself; a state of affairs.

words.tr: n. 收集者；收藏家；“collector”的复数；
words.ex: Collectors buy old coins and stamps.
words.ex_cn: 收集者购买旧硬币和邮票。
words.en: Collectors are people who collect things of a particular type as a hobby or for investment.

words.tr: v. 重新买（商品、证券等）；买回（商品、证券等）; n. 买回，购回
words.ex: The company announced plans to repurchase its shares.
words.ex_cn: 该公司宣布了回购其股份的计划。
words.en: To buy something again, especially something that you previously owned.

words.ex: The hospital discharges patients after they recover.
words.ex_cn: 医院在病人康复后让他们出院。
words.en: To release or allow to flow out; to dismiss from a job or duty.

words.ex: He finished in the thirteenth position.
words.ex_cn: 他获得了第十三名。
words.en: The ordinal number corresponding to the cardinal number thirteen.

words.ex: Constant criticism undermines her confidence.
words.ex_cn: 不断的批评削弱了她的信心。
words.en: To undermine means to weaken or damage something gradually, often in a secret or subtle way.

words.tr: v. 消灭；毁掉；清除；抹除
words.ex: The bomb will obliterate the building.
words.ex_cn: 炸弹会摧毁那栋大楼。
words.en: To obliterate something means to remove all signs of it or to destroy it completely.

words.ex: The car has 200 horsepower.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车有200马力。
words.en: A unit of power equal to 550 foot-pounds per second (about 750 watts), used in measuring the power of engines or motors.

words.ex: He lives a life of asceticism, eating little and owning few things.
words.ex_cn: 他过着苦行的生活，吃得少，拥有的东西也很少。
words.en: The practice of severe self-discipline and abstention from all forms of indulgence, typically for religious reasons.

words.tr: n. 荒凉；凄凉；悲痛；孤立无援
words.ex: The abandoned town was full of desolation.
words.ex_cn: 这座废弃的城镇满是荒凉。
words.en: Desolation refers to a state of complete emptiness or destruction, often evoking a sense of loneliness or despair.

words.tr: n. 出版商；出版公司；出版社（publisher 的复数）；
words.ex: The publishers released a new book last month.
words.ex_cn: 出版商上个月发布了一本新书。
words.en: Publishers are companies or individuals that prepare and issue books, journals, or music for sale.

words.tr: adv. 严重地；批评地；危急地；
words.ex: The patient is critically ill.
words.ex_cn: 病人病情严重。
words.en: In a way that involves the objective analysis and judgment of the merits and faults of a work of literature, music, or art.

words.ex: The company was accused of immorality in its business practices.
words.ex_cn: 该公司被指控在商业行为中存在不道德行为。
words.en: The quality or state of being immoral; wickedness.

words.ex: His negligence caused the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他的疏忽导致了事故。
words.en: Negligence is failure to take proper care over something that you are responsible for, which might cause damage or loss.

words.tr: adj. 可出售的；适于销售的；
words.ex: This painting is marketable because many people like it.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画是可以出售的，因为很多人喜欢它。
words.en: If something is marketable, it is easy to sell because people want to buy it.

words.ex: He paraphrased the poem in simple words.
words.ex_cn: 他用简单的语言意译了这首诗。
words.en: To paraphrase means to express the meaning of something written or spoken using different words, especially to achieve greater clarity.

words.tr: adj. 积极从事的；从事某种职业的；
words.ex: He is a practising doctor who helps many patients.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位积极从事医疗工作的医生，帮助了许多病人。
words.en: Engaged in a specified profession or occupation, especially on a regular basis.

words.tr:
n. 妥协；
v. 危及；
words.ex: They reached a compromise after hours of talk.
words.ex_cn: 经过数小时的讨论，他们达成了妥协。
words.en: A compromise is an agreement between two people or groups in which each side gives up some of the things they want so that both sides are happy at the end.

words.tr: adj. 过度的；过高的；过分的；
words.ex: The restaurant charged an exorbitant price for a small salad.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅对一份小沙拉要了过高的价格。
words.en: If you describe something such as a price or fee as exorbitant, you are emphasizing that it is much higher than it should be.

words.ex: He packed his belongings before moving to a new city.
words.ex_cn: 他在搬去新城市前收拾好了自己的所有物。
words.en: Your belongings are the things that you own, especially things that are small enough to be carried.

words.ex: The view from the hill is marvellous.
words.ex_cn: 从山上看到的景色绝妙极了。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as marvellous, you are emphasizing that they are extremely good, enjoyable, or impressive.

words.tr: v. 持续存在；坚持不懈
words.ex: He is persisting despite the difficulties.
words.ex_cn: 尽管有困难，他仍在坚持。
words.en: To continue to exist or occur over a prolonged period; to continue firmly or obstinately in a course of action in spite of difficulty or opposition.

words.ex: His ostensible reason for leaving was sickness.
words.ex_cn: 他离开的表面原因是生病。
words.en: An ostensible reason or purpose seems to be the real one, but it is not.

words.tr: adj. 误导的； v. “mislead”的现在分词；
words.ex: The ad is misleading because it shows fake results.
words.ex_cn: 这个广告是误导的，因为它展示了虚假的结果。
words.en: If you describe something as misleading, you mean that it gives you a wrong idea or impression.

words.ex: His abstention helped the bill pass.
words.ex_cn: 他的弃权帮助法案通过了。
words.en: An abstention is a formal act of not voting either for or against a proposal.

words.ex: He has bronchitis and can't stop coughing.
words.ex_cn: 他得了支气管炎，一直止不住咳嗽。
words.en: Bronchitis is an illness in which the bronchial tubes become inflamed and produce a lot of mucus, causing coughing and difficulty in breathing.

words.tr: n. 食物；营养；维持生计
words.ex: Water and food are basic sustenance for life.
words.ex_cn: 水和食物是生命的基本生存物资。
words.en: Sustenance refers to the food and drink that people, animals, and plants need to live and stay healthy. It can also mean the means of maintaining life or supporting existence.

words.tr: n. 传统；传统( tradition的名词复数 )；
words.ex: Our family follows old traditions at Christmas.
words.ex_cn: 我们的家庭在圣诞节时遵循古老的习俗。
words.en: Traditions are customs or beliefs that have existed for a long time among a particular group of people.

words.tr: adj. 能获得的；可得到的
words.ex: The prize is obtainable if you win the game.
words.ex_cn: 如果你赢了比赛，这个奖品就能得到。
words.en: If something is obtainable, it is possible to get it.

words.tr: n. 牧师职位；神职人员
words.ex: He became a priest and joined the priesthood.
words.ex_cn: 他成为了一名牧师，并加入了神职人员行列。
words.en: The priesthood refers to the position or office of a priest, or the group of priests as a whole.

words.ex: The teacher gave students discretion to choose their own topic.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了学生自行选择题目的权利。
words.en: Discretion is the quality of behaving in a quiet and controlled way without drawing attention to yourself or giving away personal or private information.

words.tr: adj. 工作过度的； v. “overwork”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is overworked and needs a rest.
words.ex_cn: 他工作过度，需要休息。
words.en: If someone is overworked, they have to work too hard or too much.

words.tr: adj. 注过册的； v. 注册；登记；“register”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is a registered student at the university.
words.ex_cn: 他是这所大学的注册学生。
words.en: Officially recorded or entered in a list or register.

words.ex: The formula simplifies the problem.
words.ex_cn: 这个公式简化了问题。
words.en: To make something less complicated and therefore easier to do or understand.

words.ex: The parcelling of goods was done efficiently to ensure timely delivery.
words.ex_cn: 货物的分装工作高效完成，以确保及时交付。
words.en: The act of dividing or distributing something into parts or packages.

words.tr: n. 输送；运输；财产让与；运输工具
words.ex: The conveyance of goods took three days.
words.ex_cn: 货物的运输花了三天时间。
words.en: The act or process of transporting or carrying something from one place to another.

words.ex: He capitalised on the chance to travel abroad.
words.ex_cn: 他利用了去国外旅行的机会。
words.en: To capitalize means to take advantage of a particular opportunity or to write a letter or word in capital letters. It can also refer to providing a company with the money it needs to function.

words.ex: He remained unaffected by the noise.
words.ex_cn: 他没有受到噪音的影响。
words.en: If someone or something is unaffected by an event or occurrence, they are not changed by it in any way.

words.tr: n. 历史学家；史学工作者；历史学家，史学工作者( historian的名词复数 )；
words.ex: Historians study old letters and documents.
words.ex_cn: 历史学家研究旧信件和文件。
words.en: People who study or write about history.

words.ex: Loud music interferes with my study.
words.ex_cn: 嘈杂的音乐妨碍我学习。
words.en: If you interfere, you get involved in a situation when it is not your problem or concern.

words.ex: He is the wealthiest man in the town.
words.ex_cn: 他是这个镇上最富有的人。
words.en: The superlative form of 'wealthy', meaning having the greatest amount of wealth or riches.

words.tr: adj. 平行的；相同的；类似的
words.ex: The two roads are paralleled by a river.
words.ex_cn: 两条路与一条河流平行。
words.en: adj. Being parallel or corresponding in some way.

words.ex: He felt insecurity when he lost his job.
words.ex_cn: 当他失去工作时，他感到不安全感。
